1648|# Rust Memory Optimization Guide
1649|
1650|Advanced strategies for reducing allocations, shrinking layout sizes, and boosting performance.
1651|
1652|## Core Rules & Patterns
1653|
1654|### 1. Bounded Heap-Free Collections
1655|For collections that are usually small, avoid standard vectors to bypass heap allocations.
1656|- **`SmallVec`**: Stack-allocated up to a threshold, overflows to the heap.
1657|- **`ArrayVec`**: Fixed-capacity array wrapper; never allocates on the heap.
1658|- **`ThinVec`**: Only takes a single pointer size when empty, reducing size in enum layouts.
1659|
1660|```rust
1661|use smallvec::{smallvec, SmallVec};
1662|use arrayvec::ArrayVec;
1663|
1664|// SmallVec: Allocates 4 items on the stack. Goes to heap only if count > 4.
1665|let mut local_tags: SmallVec<[String; 4]> = smallvec![];
1666|local_tags.push("Rust".to_string());
1667|
1668|// ArrayVec: Absolute limit of 8 items on the stack. No heap overflow.
1669|let mut coordinates: ArrayVec<f64, 8> = ArrayVec::new();
1670|coordinates.push(42.0);
1671|```
1672|
1673|### 2. Small String Optimization (SSO)
1674|Standard `String` consumes 24 bytes and allocates heap space immediately. Use `CompactString` for inline small strings (under 24 bytes) without allocating.
1675|
1676|```rust
1677|use compact_str::CompactString;
1678|
1679|// No heap allocation for strings <= 24 characters
1680|let username = CompactString::new("user_123");
1681|```
1682|
1683|### 3. Boxed Slices vs Vectors
1684|If a collection's size is determined once at initialization and never changes, convert it from `Vec<T>` to `Box<[T]>` to save 8 bytes of stack capacity space.
1685|
1686|```rust
1687|let items_vec: Vec<i32> = vec![1, 2, 3];
1688|
1689|// Save capacity field (shrinks stack representation from 24 to 16 bytes)
1690|let items_slice: Box<[i32]> = items_vec.into_boxed_slice();
1691|```
1692|
1693|### 4. Zero-Copy Patterns
1694|Instead of cloning or allocating strings, hold references to existing memory using slices or crates like `bytes::Bytes`.
1695|
1696|```rust
1697|use bytes::Bytes;
1698|
1699|pub struct Message {
1700|    // Zero-copy reference-counted byte buffer slice
1701|    pub payload: Bytes,
1702|}
1703|
1704|// Can be sliced and shared among threads without cloning underlying memory
1705|let original = Bytes::from(vec![0; 1024]);
1706|let slice = original.slice(0..100); 
1707|```
1708|
1709|### 5. Arena Allocation
1710|For batch allocation where structures share a lifecycle (e.g. AST parsing), use arena allocators (`bumpalo`) to allocate items sequentially in a continuous region of memory and free them all at once.
1711|
1712|```rust
1713|use bumpalo::Bump;
1714|
1715|let bump = Bump::new();
1716|
1717|// Allocates quickly on the bump arena
1718|let string_ref = bump.alloc_str("dynamic string");
1719|let int_ref = bump.alloc(42);
1720|
1721|// Entire arena is cleared at once on drop
1722|```
1723|
1724|### 6. Collection Reuse
1725|Reuse collection allocations in performance-critical loops with `.clear()` instead of re-instantiating.
1726|
1727|```rust
1728|// Bad: Allocates a new vector every iteration
1729|for item in feed {
1730|    let mut batch = Vec::new();
1731|    batch.push(item);
1732|}
1733|
1734|// Good: Reuses allocation buffer
1735|let mut batch = Vec::with_capacity(100);
1736|for item in feed {
1737|    batch.clear();
1738|    batch.push(item);
1739|}
1740|```
1741|
1742|## Layout Awareness
1743|
1744|Use `std::mem::size_of` to understand data layout.
1745|
1746|```rust
1747|println!("User size: {}", std::mem::size_of::<User>());
1748|```
1749|
1750|Reorder fields to reduce padding only when the type is numerous or hot.
1751|
1752|```rust
1753|// Often smaller: group large-alignment fields first
1754|struct Record {
1755|    id: u64,
1756|    flags: u32,
1757|    kind: u8,
1758|}
1759|```
1760|
1761|## String Strategy
1762|
1763|```rust
1764|fn label<'a>(name: &'a str, fallback: &'a str) -> std::borrow::Cow<'a, str> {
1765|    if name.is_empty() { fallback.into() } else { name.into() }
1766|}
1767|```
1768|
1769|Avoid `format!` in tight loops. Reuse buffers with `clear()`.
1770|
1771|## Zero-Copy Parsing
1772|
1773|Return slices into the input when the input outlives parsed data.
1774|
1775|```rust
1776|pub struct Header<'a> {
1777|    pub name: &'a str,
1778|    pub value: &'a str,
1779|}
1780|```
1781|
1782|Do not force zero-copy when it creates unmanageable lifetimes for little gain.
1783|
1784|## ThinVec for Enum Payloads
1785|
1786|When enums contain `Vec` variants, `ThinVec` reduces the enum size by storing only a pointer when empty:
1787|
1788|```rust
1789|use thin_vec::ThinVec;
1790|
1791|// Regular Vec in an enum makes the enum 24+ bytes even when empty
1792|enum Node {
1793|    Leaf(i64),
1794|    Children(Vec<Node>),     // 24 bytes for Vec
1795|}
1796|
1797|// ThinVec only stores 8 bytes (a pointer) when empty
1798|enum NodeOptimized {
1799|    Leaf(i64),
1800|    Children(ThinVec<Node>), // 8 bytes for ThinVec
1801|}
1802|```
1803|
1804|## Cow for Conditional Ownership
1805|
1806|```rust
1807|use std::borrow::Cow;
1808|
1809|pub struct Error {
1810|    message: Cow<'static, str>,
1811|}
1812|
1813|impl Error {
1814|    // No allocation for static messages
1815|    pub fn new(msg: &'static str) -> Self {
1816|        Self { message: Cow::Borrowed(msg) }
1817|    }
1818|
1819|    // Allocates only when dynamic
1820|    pub fn with_detail(msg: String) -> Self {
1821|        Self { message: Cow::Owned(msg) }
1822|    }
1823|}
1824|```
1825|
1826|## Arc vs Rc Trade-offs
1827|
1828|```rust
1829|use std::rc::Rc;
1830|use std::sync::Arc;
1831|
1832|// Single-threaded shared ownership — cheaper than Arc
1833|let shared = Rc::new(large_data);
1834|
1835|// Multi-threaded shared ownership — required across threads
1836|let shared = Arc::new(large_data);
1837|```
1838|
1839|Prefer `Rc` when data never crosses thread boundaries. `Arc` adds atomic reference counting overhead.
1840|
1841|## HashMap Memory Optimization
1842|
1843|```rust
1844|use hashbrown::HashMap;
1845|
1846|// hashbrown's HashMap uses less memory than std's and is faster
1847|let mut map: HashMap<String, i32> = HashMap::with_capacity(128);
1848|
1849|// Reserve capacity upfront to avoid rehashing
1850|map.reserve(expected_count);
1851|
1852|// Consider FxHashMap for non-adversarial keys
1853|use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
1854|let mut fast_map: FxHashMap<String, i32> = FxHashMap::default();
1855|```
1856|
1857|## Stack vs Heap Decision Matrix
1858|
1859|| Type | Stack Size | Heap Alloc | Use When |
1860||------|-----------|------------|----------|
1861|| `String` | 24 bytes | Yes | Owns mutable text |
1862|| `&str` | 16 bytes | No | Borrowed text, lifetime bound |
1863|| `CompactString` | 24 bytes | No (≤24 chars) | Short strings that own data |
1864|| `Cow<str>` | 32 bytes | Conditionally | Mostly static, rarely dynamic |
1865|| `Box<str>` | 16 bytes | Yes | Owned fixed string |
1866|| `Vec<T>` | 24 bytes | Yes | Growable collection |
1867|| `SmallVec<[T; N]>` | ~24+ bytes | Only if >N | Usually small, occasionally large |
1868|| `Box<[T]>` | 16 bytes | Yes | Fixed-size after construction |
1869|| `ThinVec<T>` | 8 bytes | Only if non-empty | Empty or small in enums |
1870|
1871|## Measuring Memory
1872|
1873|```rust
1874|use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, System, Layout};
1875|
1876|struct TrackingAllocator;
1877|
1878|unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for TrackingAllocator {
1879|    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
1880|        System.alloc(layout)
1881|    }
1882|
1883|    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
1884|        System.dealloc(ptr, layout)
1885|    }
1886|}
1887|
1888|// For detailed profiling, use dhat, heaptrack, or valgrind
1889|```
1890|
1891|Use `dhat` crate for heap profiling in tests:
1892|
1893|```rust
1894|#[cfg(test)]
1895|mod tests {
1896|    #[test]
1897|    fn memory_test() {
1898|        let _profiler = dhat::Profiler::new_heap();
1899|        // code under test
1900|        // dhat prints allocation stats on drop
1901|    }
1902|}
1903|```
1904|
1905|## Optimization Workflow
1906|
1907|1. Measure allocations and CPU first.
1908|2. Identify the hot path and expected data sizes.
1909|3. Pick the narrowest memory change.
1910|4. Benchmark before/after.
1911|5. Keep readability unless the win is meaningful.
1912|
1913|## Allocation Decision Rules
1914|
1915|- `Vec<T>`: general purpose growable collection.
1916|- `SmallVec<[T; N]>`: usually-small collection with occasional heap spill.
1917|- `ArrayVec<T, N>`: hard maximum size, no heap allocation.
1918|- `Box<[T]>`: fixed-size heap slice after construction.
1919|- `Bytes`: shared immutable byte buffers.
1920|- `Bump`: many same-lifetime allocations.
1921|- `Cow<'a, T>`: borrow unless mutation/ownership is required.
1922|
1923|## Anti-Patterns
1924|
1925|```rust
1926|// Bad: cloning a large Vec just to avoid lifetime complexity
1927|let data = original.clone(); // expensive and unnecessary
1928|
1929|// Good: use Arc or Cow for shared ownership
1930|let data: Arc<[u8]> = original.into();
1931|```
1932|
1933|```rust
1934|// Bad: allocating inside a hot loop
1935|for item in items {
1936|    let s = format!("processing {}", item); // allocates every iteration
1937|}
1938|
1939|// Good: reuse a buffer
1940|let mut buf = String::with_capacity(128);
1941|for item in items {
1942|    buf.clear();
1943|    write!(buf, "processing {}", item).unwrap();
1944|}
1945|```
1946|
1947|- Replacing every `Vec` with `SmallVec` without measuring.
1948|- Keeping arena references after reset.
1949|- Cloning strings to satisfy ownership instead of shortening borrow scopes.
1950|- Using `Arc` as a default clone workaround.
1951|- Optimizing layout for types created a handful of times.
1952|- Using `Box<dyn Trait>` when generics would eliminate the allocation entirely.
1953|
1954|## Review Prompt
1955|
1956|When reviewing memory optimization, ask what was measured, which allocation is removed, what lifetime assumptions changed, and whether the new type increases stack size or API complexity.
1957|
1958|## Optimization Checklist
1959|
1960|- Measure allocations before changing data structures.
1961|- Preallocate collections only when capacity is known or bounded.
1962|- Prefer borrowing and `Cow` before cloning strings or buffers.
1963|- Use arenas only when lifetimes are truly batch-scoped.
1964|- Check stack growth when replacing heap allocations with inline storage.
1965|- Re-benchmark after changes and keep the simpler version if gains are noise.
1966|- Profile with `dhat` or `heaptrack` to find actual allocation hotspots.
1967|- Consider `hashbrown` or `rustc-hash` for HashMap-heavy code.

1999|## Core Concepts
2000|
2001|### 1. Memory Bug Categories
2002|
2003|| Bug Type             | Description                      | Prevention        |
2004|| -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------- |
2005|| **Use-after-free**   | Access freed memory              | Ownership, RAII   |
2006|| **Double-free**      | Free same memory twice           | Smart pointers    |
2007|| **Memory leak**      | Never free memory                | RAII, GC          |
2008|| **Buffer overflow**  | Write past buffer end            | Bounds checking   |
2009|| **Dangling pointer** | Pointer to freed memory          | Lifetime tracking |
2010|| **Data race**        | Concurrent unsynchronized access | Ownership, Sync   |
2011|
2012|### 2. Safety Spectrum
2013|
2014|```
2015|Manual (C) → Smart Pointers (C++) → Ownership (Rust) → GC (Go, Java)
2016|Less safe                                              More safe
2017|More control                                           Less control
2018|```

2024|## Best Practices
2025|
2026|### Do's
2027|
2028|- **Prefer RAII** - Tie resource lifetime to scope
2029|- **Use smart pointers** - Avoid raw pointers in C++
2030|- **Understand ownership** - Know who owns what
2031|- **Check bounds** - Use safe access methods
2032|- **Use tools** - AddressSanitizer, Valgrind, Miri
2033|
2034|### Don'ts
2035|
2036|- **Don't use raw pointers** - Unless interfacing with C
2037|- **Don't return local references** - Dangling pointer
2038|- **Don't ignore compiler warnings** - They catch bugs
2039|- **Don't use `unsafe` carelessly** - In Rust, minimize it
